_comment: Importable Orcabot dashboard template. Unlike the other benchmark templates this one needs no orchestrator, no agent and no API key: the terminal's boot command runs the whole benchmark and serves its report on localhost, and the browser block is pointed at that server. Seed with bin/seed-benchmark-templates.
name: TTS Benchmark Runner
description: Run the open-weight TTS benchmark and read its report

items.content:
{"name": "TTS benchmark", "agentic": false, "bootCommand": "PORT=8099 # talkito refuses to fetch model weights when it cannot ask a human. The picker # below is interactive, but the download prompt would land in the middle of a # sweep the reader has walked away from, so it is answered in advance. export TALKITO_AUTO_APPROVE_DOWNLOADS=1 ROOT=/workspace/talkito BENCH=$ROOT/benchmark SERVE=/workspace/tts-report echo "== Orcabot: talkito TTS benchmark ==" # Serve a placeholder first, so the browser block has something at a stable URL from # the first second rather than an error until the run finishes. mkdir -p "$SERVE" [ -f "$SERVE/index.html" ] || printf '%s' 'TTS benchmark

Waiting for a run...

Pick engines in the terminal. This page reloads every 10 seconds and the report replaces it when the run finishes.

' > "$SERVE/index.html" curl -sf -o /dev/null --max-time 2 "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/" || ( cd "$SERVE" && nohup python3 -m http.server "$PORT" >/workspace/.tts-serve.log 2>&1 & ) # talkito's .gitmodules uses git@github.com: URLs and the sandbox has no SSH key, # so --recurse-submodules fails; both repos are cloned over HTTPS instead. # The harness ships inside talkito-benchmark, so tests-repo is not needed -- but # tools/paths.py still wants a talkito CHECKOUT (it looks for talkito/tts.py, not # the installed package), and benchmark/ inside talkito/ is the layout it resolves. [ -d "$ROOT/.git" ] || git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/robdmac/talkito.git "$ROOT" [ -d "$BENCH/.git" ] || git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/robdmac/talkito-benchmark.git "$BENCH" # make_samples.py shells out to ffmpeg for the listening clip, and the sandbox image # ships without it. Missing, the sweep still scores normally and only the play button # is lost -- but that is most of the point of the page. command -v ffmpeg >/dev/null 2>&1 || { apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq --no-install-recommends ffmpeg; } # piper needs no torch at all, and faster-whisper scores on CPU through CTranslate2, # so the cheapest arm installs in seconds. Heavier engines pull their own weights on # first use and the picker warns what each has cost before. python3 -c 'import piper' 2>/dev/null || pip3 install --break-system-packages -q piper-tts python3 -c 'import faster_whisper' 2>/dev/null || pip3 install --break-system-packages -q faster-whisper cd "$BENCH" || exec bash cat <<'BANNER' Everything is selected by default and a full sweep is around eleven hours. Press n to clear, then space to pick a few. piper alone takes about three minutes. BANNER # No --only: this is the interactive picker, and a terminal block is a real PTY, so # the arrow-key menu works exactly as it does on a laptop. python3 tools/benchmark.py rc=$? # benchmark.py sweeps and builds the page, but never synthesizes the one listening # clip per engine that the page embeds - so the table it just built has nothing to # play. Which engines to sample is only known now, after the reader has chosen, so # they are read back out of the state the sweep wrote and the page is rebuilt. MEASURED=$(python3 -c "import json;print(' '.join(sorted({k.split('|')[0] for k in json.load(open('tools/sweep_rerun.json'))['units']})))" 2>/dev/null) if [ -n "$MEASURED" ]; then echo "== adding listening clips for: $MEASURED ==" python3 tools/make_samples.py $MEASURED # build_benchmark_page.py substitutes into an existing page rather than writing # one, and benchmark.py only seeds that page on a run it actually completes. Quit # the picker with prior measurements on disk and there is nothing to substitute # into, so it dies on FileNotFoundError with every clip already synthesized. [ -f tts-benchmark.html ] || cp tools/page_template.html tts-benchmark.html python3 tools/build_benchmark_page.py tts-benchmark.html python3 tools/build_export.py tts-benchmark-export.zip tts-benchmark.html fi if [ -f tts-benchmark.html ]; then cp -f tts-benchmark.html "$SERVE/index.html" echo "report published -> http://localhost:$PORT/" else echo "no tts-benchmark.html was produced; measurements (if any) are under $BENCH/tools/" fi echo "[tts benchmark done rc=$rc]" exec bash", "subagentIds": [], "skillIds": [], "mcpToolIds": []}

setupGuide:
# TTS benchmark (you are Orcabot chat)

**This dashboard is already complete. Do not set anything up.**

The template provisions both blocks and the terminal's boot command does the entire
job by itself: it clones the benchmark, installs what it needs, starts a local web
server, opens the engine picker, and publishes the report to that server when the run
finishes.

## Do not create anything

**Do NOT call create_terminal. Do NOT call create_browser.** There is already one of
each on the canvas. Creating more gives the reader two terminals and two browsers,
with a second benchmark running against the same workspace as the first -- both
writing the same measurement files, which corrupts the run rather than doubling it.

There are no keys to set, no secrets to add, no provider to choose, and no config file
to write. This benchmark makes no LLM calls and needs no API key at all.

If the reader says "walk me through setting up this dashboard", the correct answer is
that there is nothing to set up: the terminal is already doing it, and the picker is
waiting for them.

## What the reader is looking at

The terminal opens a checklist of every engine the benchmark knows. Arrows move, space
toggles, `n` clears the selection, `a` selects all, Enter starts, `q` quits. Everything
is ticked by default and the picker shows what each engine cost on previous runs.

Tell them to press `n` first unless they mean it: a full sweep is around eleven hours,
and longer on a first run because each engine downloads its own weights. piper alone is
about three minutes and is the cheapest complete arm in the table.

The browser block shows a placeholder that reloads every ten seconds, and the report
replaces it when the run finishes.

## Answering "how is it going?"

Read the terminal. Each engine prints a line per category as it completes, then a
summary line of the form `piper 82/84 phrases WER 5.0% RTF 0.07x`. The run ends with
`[tts benchmark done rc=N]`; a non-zero `rc` means at least one engine failed and the
per-engine output above says which.

Measurements are saved per unit as they complete, so an interrupted run keeps its
finished work and starting again resumes rather than restarting.

## If they want to re-run or change the selection

They type `python3 tools/benchmark.py` in the same terminal -- it drops to a shell in
the right directory when the run ends. `--keep` adds to the existing measurements
instead of replacing the ones for the engines they pick. The page and the export can
always be rebuilt from stored measurements alone:

    python3 tools/build_benchmark_page.py tts-benchmark.html
